newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash prods mixed before API, gasoline slumps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash prods mixed before API, gasoline slumps.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices were mixed in afternoon dealings, with gasoline sliding and heating oil and other distillates edging higher.
But market players said discussions were very light througout the day, especially with the API inventory report due for release this afternoon.
They attributed the slack activity level to the expiration of August product's contracts on Friday and to general late-summer malaise.

The primary news item in the market was Hurricane Edouard, currently packing winds of 130 miles per hour as it moves toward the U.S. East Coast. But at least one weather expert predicted that it will not be a threat to business interests at least until the weekend, if at all.
Smith barney's Jon Davis said, however, there was a chance the storm, now about 1200 miles east of Miami, could become a threat to certain business interest on the East Coast.

New York Harbor conventional unleaded M2-grade gasoline was bid about 2.75 cents below the print, stable with Monday, traders said, adding that Buckeye barrels were trading at a premium due to congestion on the line.
Distillate diffs were about 0.25 cent a gallow weaker.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
